approach:
Add one reading check, `check_environment_reach(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, modelled on `check_code_survey` (label-prefixed assumption, gating on capability and no question), and register it as a single `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_outcome_state`. The check reads only the reading (deliverable paths, criteria, summary, assumptions), never the request or the repo. It finds two triggers. (A) Site-action: a deliverable under `.github/workflows/`, or a criterion naming a push, `origin`, `remote`, `gh`, or a pull request. (B) Unreachable source: a criterion or the summary citing job records, job or commit or git history, the records branch or `athena/records` as a source. A reading with a trigger must carry an `Environment:` assumption that names a site (CI job, runner, producer snapshot, local, host and so on), a permission (read or write) and the data or refs reached. For a host action (push, origin, remote, gh, pull request) it must also state the no-origin case. For case B it must also quote at least one figure inline or name a reachable file path, which is not under records/ or athena/records. The doc comment names the root cause and the three jobs. The reader brief gets one rule line, and the corpus gets refuse and accept cases. Two existing tests that accepted workflow deliverables get an `Environment:` assumption. Nothing else changes: no record schema, no data file, no prompt file, no governance file.

Root cause, as the doc comment and changelog will state it: the reading stage had no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches. The check lives at the reading gate because that is the stage that assigns the actions. It is a gate step and not a patch for one job.

decisions.choice: Implement the rule as a lexical check on the reading's own fields, with the `Environment:` assumption label, in `refusing_check` as one `step!` line placed after `check_outcome_state`.
decisions.reason: `check_code_survey` (reading.rs:3910) and `check_design_existing_code` (reading.rs:4033) already enforce a label-prefixed assumption the same way, with no model call and no repo read. A `step!` line is what the corpus mechanism (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, refusal_corpus.rs:1061) tracks. After outcome_state keeps the test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` (reading.rs:7725), which pins outcome_state right after governance, passing. It also leaves the anchor line `step!(check_reading_references(` that `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` (refusal_corpus.rs:1083) needs.

rejected.option: Add an `environment` field to the Reading record
rejected.why: It changes the record schema (`deny_unknown_fields`, records.rs:444) and the reader output schema, and touches stored records. The request says no record or data file is added.

rejected.option: A checked-in environment-capabilities table file, as introspection 20261024-220314-yjtg proposed
rejected.why: Out of scope: the brief excludes any table, record or data file. The reader states the environment per reading, and the gate checks that it did.
That check applies only to class code or tests with a behavior criterion. Job 20261025-034247-nm0k was a docs reading, and a workflow deliverable can sit in any class.

The action is assigned in the reading's criteria and deliverables, so that is where to look. Request words already feed the governance and outcome checks, and a request may mention push without the reading assigning it.
The `Environment:` assumption itself must say push, origin and records, so scanning it would trigger on its own repair text.

decisions.choice: Trigger A fires on a deliverable path starting `.github/workflows/` (any action) or a criterion word: push, pushes, pushed, pushing, origin, remote, remotes, gh, or the pair pull + request(s). Words are whole lowercase alphanumeric tokens.
decisions.reason: This matches the two environment-dependent shapes in the brief (CI workflow, external host action). Whole-token matching keeps `originates`, `ghost`, `pushdown` and `remotely` from triggering. No reading fixture in the repo that is accepted through the gate has these words in a criterion or summary; I grepped reading.rs, the corpus, the fake reader and the CLI test helpers. The two tests that do have workflow deliverables (reading.rs:7451, 7492) are updated.

rejected.why: `origin` would hit 'originates', and the root-cause bullet 'fixed where it originates' sits in the corpus's root_cause_request, so it would refuse an unrelated reading.

rejected.option: Include the bare word `records` or the path `records/` in trigger B
rejected.why: Too common (`AnyRecord`, 'records validation'). B uses the phrases job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch and athena/records.

decisions.choice: An `Environment:` assumption is complete when its own words hold a site word, a permission word and a data word from three fixed lists. A host action also needs the origin word with a no/without/missing/absent/none/non word. Case B also needs a number of 1–5 digits (a quoted figure) or a file path with a data/doc extension that is not under records/ or athena/records.
decisions.reason: A mechanical test of 'who/where, what permissions, what data reached' that the reader can satisfy from one sentence, and a refusal text that names which part is missing. The 1–5 digit limit avoids counting the 6- and 8-digit parts of a job id as a figure. The host-action case list carries the 20261025-070538-8ra0 prevention (no origin, non-GitHub origin, GitHub origin). The inline-or-file rule carries the 20261025-034247-nm0k prevention.

rejected.why: The reader could write 'Environment: fine' and the gate would pass a reading that never says who runs it or what it reaches.

rejected.option: A free-text judge by a model call
rejected.why: It adds cost and non-determinism to a gate that today runs no model call, and it is hard to pin in the corpus.

decisions.choice: Add one rule line to `READING_RULES` in briefs.rs (array length 6 to 7) and update the briefs.rs tests that count it. The line is at most 220 characters; the existing test caps rule lines at 220.
decisions.reason: The reader writes the assumption only if told. The briefs sit outside the budgeted prompt sets (system-facts: 'Their briefs ... sit outside these sets'), so the budget lines in docs/system-facts.md do not move. Prompt files are not edited because the reader set is 1997 of 2000.

rejected.why: No token headroom (budget reader: 1997 of 2000), and prompt files are out of scope.

steps: In reading.rs next to `check_code_survey` (line ~3910), add `environment_assumptions(reading)` (assumptions whose trimmed text starts with 'environment:' in any case, as `code_surveys` at line 3828 does), a lowercase alphanumeric tokenizer, the three word lists (site, permission, data), the host-action detector (push/pushes/pushed/pushing, origin, remote, remotes, gh, or pull followed by request/requests, whole tokens over criteria text), the workflow detector (a deliverable path starting `.github/workflows/`, any action), the unreachable-source detector (token-sequence phrases job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, athena records, over criteria and the summary), and `names_reachable_file` / `quotes_figures` for case B (a file token with a .md/.json/.jsonl/.txt/.csv/.toml/.rs/.yml/.yaml extension that is not under records/ or athena/records; or a purely numeric token of 1–5 digits).

Add `pub fn check_environment_reach(reading: &Reading) -> Result<()>`. It returns Ok when the capability is None, a question is set, or no trigger fires. Otherwise it needs one complete `Environment:` assumption: a site word, a permission word and a data word; for a host action also the origin-or-remote word with a no/without/missing/absent/none/non word; for case B also a quoted figure or a reachable file. The doc comment follows the style of `check_code_survey`: root cause (no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches), the three jobs, the triggers, the limits (lexical; the bare word `records` is not a trigger), the replay hold sentences ('This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'expected 8% of newly refused readings'), and what the error says. risks.risk: False positives: a docs or code reading that mentions 'push' or 'remote' in a criterion for an unrelated reason is refused.
risks.mitigation: Triggers are whole-token matches on criteria, the summary and deliverable paths. They skip assumptions, out_of_scope and the request text. The accept tests in criterion 6 cover 'originates', 'ghost', 'pushdown' and 'remotely'. The declared share of 8% is for the replay hold, and a full `cargo test --workspace` run checks the fixtures in every crate.

risks.risk: The lexical lists are gameable: an `Environment:` sentence can hold the right words and still be wrong.
risks.mitigation: The check cannot know the facts; it only makes the reader state them. The three word lists and the figure/file rule are fixed and tested, and the refusal text names exactly what is missing. The doc comment states that the check is lexical, which is the same level of check as the 'Code survey:' rule. A later change can tighten the lists, with cases.

risks.risk: Existing tests that accept workflow-deliverable readings fail once the step exists.
risks.mitigation: The plan lists those two tests (reading.rs:7451, 7492) as edits. The producer must run `cargo test -p athena-core` and fix any other fixture the run reveals with an `Environment:` assumption, not by weakening the check.

risks.risk: The new rule line pushes the briefs.rs rule section over its size bound or the 220-byte cap.
risks.mitigation: The brief's own test caps rule lines at 220 bytes and the section size is bounded. The producer measures the section size, sets the bound just above it, and keeps the line short. The line is: 'Environment: an action on CI, a push or pull request, or a source in job records or history needs an `Environment:` assumption naming site, read/write permissions and data it reaches (`check_environment_reach`).'

risks.risk: The new text trips the boundary scan (banned words about who runs Athena) or the personal-data allow-list.
risks.mitigation: The check reads only deliverable paths, criteria, summary and assumptions, as `check_code_survey` does. The producer must not paraphrase who runs Athena in any new text. The word lists use CI and host vocabulary (ci, runner, producer, snapshot, local, host, github) and avoid the banned list, and the full workspace test run includes the boundary scan.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused by an earlier check (governance, repo paths, references) and so does not exercise the new step.
risks.mitigation: The corpus accept cases use only docs/design/roadmap.md, which is in `repo_files()` (refusal_corpus.rs:173). The workflow case uses a Create deliverable, so `check_boundary_and_repo_files` does not need the file to exist. Each case changes one field of `base_reading` so no earlier check refuses first, and the producer verifies each refuse case names `check_environment_reach` and not an earlier check.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in reading.rs `mod tests`. Each builds a `Reading` with `governed_reading` and `add_behavior` (both exist, reading.rs:7364 and 7505) and calls the public `refusing_check` (exists, reading.rs:3226). The cases: (i) a deliverable `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (Create) named in a criterion, no Environment assumption: the refusing check is `check_environment_reach`, and the error starts 'the reading was refused because' and names site, permissions and data. demonstrations.method: Unit tests with three readings shaped like the three jobs. (engm) A code-class reading with a `Code survey:` assumption, so check_code_survey passes, whose criterion says 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch'. Without an Environment assumption it is refused. A complete Environment assumption with no figure or file is still refused (the error says 'quote the figures inline or name a reachable file'). A complete one that says CI has read-only contents and cannot write the records branch, and quotes '3 jobs, 12 readings', is accepted. (8ra0) The push/origin/pull-request reading from criterion 3, accepted only when the no-origin case is stated. (nm0k) A docs reading whose summary says 'Use figures from job records and history' is refused. It is accepted when the Environment assumption quotes the figures inline, and when it lists the file docs/design/roadmap.md instead. An assumption listing only records/foo.json or athena/records/x.json as the file is refused. Each of the three readings is also checked through `refusing_check` so the refusing check's name is `check_environment_reach`. A loop covers every B phrase: job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, athena/records.
demonstrations.observes: A reading citing records or history as a source is refused unless the figures are inline or a reachable file is listed, and is accepted when they are. Three differently shaped readings are covered, so the class is tested and not one job.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the name assertions fail. Without the figure/file rule, the 'complete but nothing quoted' reading is wrongly accepted.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests plus corpus accept cases. A plain docs reading (`governed_reading(&["docs/x.md"], &["docs/x.md exists"], &[])`) passes `check_environment_reach` and `refusing_check` returns None. Readings with trigger words only inside other words ('fixed where it originates', 'ghost', 'pushdown', 'remotely', 'history of the page' with no trigger phrase) pass. A declined reading (capability None), a reading with a question, and one with no deliverables pass even with a push criterion. Existing accept tests keep passing, with `Environment:` assumptions added only to the two workflow-deliverable tests (reading.rs:7451, 7492). The declared-share wording is pinned by the doc/changelog test from criterion 5.
demonstrations.observes: Docs-only readings and readings without a trigger are accepted. The 8% declaration is present in the doc comment and the changelog.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the triggers were substring matches, 'originates' would be refused and the accept test would fail. If the gating on capability and question were missing, the declined and question readings would be refused.
